about.title: Swedish first aid know-how, taught in Bangladesh.
about.text: We are the Bangladesh branch of Första Hjälpencentrum, a Swedish private company that has trained people in first aid since 1989. Our aim is simple: help people feel confident giving care in the minutes before professional help arrives.
points: Certified trainers, teaching in Bangla and English
Courses designed to meet Bangladesh labour-law workplace safety requirements

training.title: One standard. Eight worlds.
training.intro: Every course is tailored to the risks your people actually face.

sectors.title: General
sectors.audience: Adults (high and low risk), children, infants and toddlers
sectors.topics: Recovery position, CPR with defibrillation, choking, drowning, bleeding, fractures, burns, poisoning, stroke, heart attack, epilepsy, diabetes, fever

sectors.title: Corporate
sectors.audience: Banks, insurance, financial services, IT, telecom, hotels, multinationals
sectors.topics: Workplace emergencies, CPR and AED, choking, bleeding, burns, sudden illness

sectors.title: Construction & Industry
sectors.audience: Garments, power and energy, real estate
sectors.topics: Head injuries, amputation, heat stroke, shock, fractures, severe bleeding

sectors.title: Defence & Law Enforcement
sectors.topics: Penetrating injuries (knife, gunshot, explosion), tourniquets, trauma care

sectors.title: Embassies & Foreign Organisations
sectors.topics: CPR and AED, medical emergencies, travel and field first aid

sectors.title: Medical
sectors.audience: Doctors, nurses, interns, medical students, midwives, hospital staff, nannies
sectors.topics: Basic Life Support (BLS), CPR and AED, airway management

sectors.title: Transport
sectors.topics: In-transit emergencies, CPR and AED, choking, sudden illness

lab.title: Watch it. Learn it. Feel the beat.
lab.intro: Tap a scenario to see the key steps in motion.
lab.disclaimer: These animations are for awareness only. They don't replace hands-on certified training. In an emergency in Bangladesh, call 999.

scenes.title: CPR
steps: 30 hard, fast chest compressions (100–120 a minute, 5–6 cm deep)

scenes.title: AED
steps: Switch on the AED and follow the voice
Attach the pads to the bare chest
Press shock if advised, then restart CPR

scenes.title: Recovery position
steps: Arm nearest you at a right angle
Roll onto the side and tilt the head back

scenes.title: Choking
steps: Repeat; call 999 if it doesn't clear

scenes.title: Severe bleeding
steps: Call 999; use a tourniquet if trained

scenes.title: Burns
steps: Cool under running water for 20 minutes

trainer.title: Can you keep the CPR beat?
trainer.text: Tap the chest (or press Space) at 100–120 compressions a minute. Do 30 and see your score.

members.name: Jonas Wikström
members.bio: Specialist in anaesthesia and intensive care with more than 25 years in pre-hospital and emergency medicine. Founded the company in 1989, master trainer for the Swedish Resuscitation Council since 1992, and author of three books on emergency medicine.
